headline: WASDE PRINTS AT 11 CT: WHEAT LEADS, BEANS REACT
subheadline: Wheat ran 10 cents into the report; soybean oil is the quiet mover nobody's talking about yet.
lead: Chicago wheat pushed up 10 cents to $6.45 this morning, the loudest pre-WASDE move in the complex, and it's not an accident. A possible Black Sea deal is circulating in the overnight wires, which is exactly the kind of headline that gets fund desks repositioning before an 11 CT print that could reset global wheat supply. The WASDE lands in hours. Everything this morning is positioning.
the_takeaway: Wheat is the tell heading into 11 CT; beans react after the number prints.
teaser: Wheat runs a dime into the WASDE. The report answers why at 11 CT.

one_number.unit: vessels transiting Hormuz Tuesday, a weekly low
one_number.context: Shipping data shows only 8 vessels moved through the Strait of Hormuz in either direction Tuesday as the US-Iran standoff dragged into a second week. With Brent topping $89 overnight, WTI's $82.92 close is lagging the risk premium the front month usually carries in these cycles.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans down, toward below $11.74. Nearby beans closed $11.55 today, down from yesterday's implied level.
yesterdays_call.note: Directional and level both resolved; old-crop beans gave back more than the call required, though the Nov contract barely moved.

sections.title: WHEAT LEADS INTO THE PRINT
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat added **10 cents** to $6.45, the sharpest pre-report move in the grain complex, driven by overnight chatter about a possible Black Sea deal that could bring Russian supply back into the global bid.
- A Black Sea agreement, if it materializes, adds bushels to a world balance sheet the WASDE is about to update; the fund desks repositioning ahead of 11 CT are pricing that risk, not a confirmed outcome.
- $6.45 is the upper edge of the five-session range; the WASDE either gives wheat a reason to hold that ground or hands it back fast.
sections.catalyst: Agweb: possible Black Sea deal circulating overnight, repositioning ahead of WASDE.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat ran on a rumor. The report decides if the rumor was priced correctly.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: yesterday's flat session gave way to the complex's loudest pre-WASDE move.

sections.title: BEANS SPLIT: OLD CROP FIRMS, NEW CROP FLAT
sections.body:
- Nearby beans added 7 cents to **$11.55**, old-crop positioning ahead of the WASDE; Nov '26 barely moved at **$11.72**.
- Soybean oil outran the rest of the complex -- see TMYK below for why that matters to crush economics.
- Yesterday's action flagged $11.78 as the target for unpriced new-crop beans; Nov at $11.72 says the market hasn't offered that yet. The 11 CT print is the next real chance.
sections.bottom_line: Old crop doing the work; new crop is waiting on 11 CT, and $11.78 is the number that reopens the sale window.

sections.title: CORN TICKS; WASDE IS THE ONLY STORY
sections.body:
- Corn nearby added a penny and a half to **$4.40**, Dec '26 to $4.63; neither number says anything new.
- The weekly thread question is whether the WASDE confirms a record or near-record yield and breaks Dec below $4.50; that answer comes at 11 CT, not in this morning's half-cent drift.
sections.catalyst: No clean catalyst for the morning tick; all positioning is WASDE-driven.
sections.bottom_line: Dec $4.50 is the line the report either defends or loses.

sections.title: CATTLE FLAT; JBS SOUDERTON MATTERS MORE
sections.body:
- Live cattle sat unchanged at **$232.75**, feeders eased fractionally to $349.98; the fed trade hasn't reset and neither contract has reason to move before direct business clears.
- JBS announced it will shut beef processing at its Souderton, PA plant Aug. 14 and convert it to value-added case-ready work after a $30M investment; combined with the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, that removes additional daily processing capacity from a market already constrained on the kill side.
sections.catalyst: JBS Souderton beef processing shutdown Aug. 14; Cargill lockout still removing roughly 6,000 head daily.
sections.bottom_line: Two processing capacity losses in the same week; watch box-beef cutout for the first response.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA Screwworm Sterile Fly Facility Opens 7 Months Early
outside_the_pit.body: A Texas facility to breed sterile flies for screwworm control will open well ahead of schedule, accelerating the eradication program that underpins the Aug. 24 phased border reopening at Douglas, AZ. Faster capacity means the reopening timeline could hold or even pull forward, which matters for feeder supply and the feeder/live spread heading into fall.

outside_the_pit.title: Fertilizer and Diesel Prices Higher Heading Into Fall Harvest
outside_the_pit.body: FarmDoc Daily reports both fertilizer and diesel are running above the prior two-year average as fall fieldwork approaches. Producers locking fall anhydrous now are paying more than 2024 or 2025 buyers did; with the Iran-Hormuz cycle keeping crude unsettled, diesel tightness is the input-cost story that hits combines and grain dryers first.

weekly_thread.question: Does the WASDE on Tuesday confirm a record or near-record corn yield, and does that break Dec corn below $4.50?
weekly_thread.status_text: The WASDE prints at 11:00 AM CT today; Dec corn at $4.63 this morning means the $4.50 line has not broken yet. The report decides.

the_more_you_know.title: Soybean Oil's Quiet Takeover of the Crush
the_more_you_know.body: Soybean oil is up 2.1% today while meal added half a percent. When oil's share of crush value expands, processors favor running the crush harder, which pulls more beans through the system. At $69.62, oil is near the top of its 52-week range; if the WASDE shows tight old-crop bean stocks, the oil share story gets a second leg.

watch_list.desc: WASDE: Dec corn above $4.50 after the print means the yield number didn't break the market; below $4.50 confirms a record yield priced in. Beans: Nov above $11.78 reopens the unpriced new-crop sale window.
Weekly export sales: soy under 300K MT keeps fund positioning, not demand, in charge of the Nov contract.
JBS Souderton processing shutdown; watch box-beef cutout for first impact on available supply.
First phased Mexican feeder cattle imports resume at Douglas, AZ; feeder/live spread is the tell as that date closes in.
